notes.title: Update Notes For v0.67.00 - IPOs, Bankruptcies and Desperate Acts
notes.notes:
[h3]Creating Public Companies[/h3]
Create your own public companies by combining your businesses and real estate, and list them on the stock market! You will be given 25% ownership in the new entity while 75% is offered to the public. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44216768/ef1fe0b59fcabd85d048ee0772b03206a47125bc.png[/img]

Once a company is listed, you lose control of the individual assets and it will behave like any other company on the stock market.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44216768/bf5e5481861ab00ec3c190e887eef5b1930ece3a.png[/img]

Keep in mind, all the extra investment money flowing into the new company will increase the related Competition Indexes - so be careful not to end up competing with your own businesses.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44216768/71a19d8065312ec9cdcc95676506c77fc8c54b95.png[/img]


[h3]Bankruptcy and Desperate Acts[/h3]
I've seen a bit of feedback that the stock market feels like too much of a gamble when a bankrupted stock wipes out your entire investment. This update introduces changes to give some warning and smaller losses before a complete wipeout can occur.

Before going bankrupt, a listed company will perform a "desperate act" to try and save itself.

Larger companies will downsize operations, causing a sudden reduction in equity per share but (hopefully) stabilising the company at a lower valuation.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44216768/921cf6e1337e39e1cb4f8eee84b8aacc628940e8.png[/img]

Smaller companies will raise capital, diluting the percentage ownership of existing shareholders. This also reduces equity per share since the new shareholders are able to invest at advantageous prices.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44216768/8febb8d318ba5788fcf41584e86edd5dce167b51.png[/img]

If you are invested in a company and they perform a desperate act, you will be notified in the monthly summary window.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44216768/e5c07dda93c49064574d24fcf56e1b551a7d7b28.png[/img]

Bankruptcy only occurs if the company needs to perform another desperate act within 6 months of the last one. Performing the Research Stock activity will tell you if the company is at risk.

[h3]Economy Changes[/h3]
Some changes to the economic model in this update - the Industry Stability difficulty slider has been replaced by an Economy Stability difficulty slider. This introduces economy-wide crashes that will affect many industries at the same time. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44216768/36f275b9322df1e38d812ac6f9cd76feee842e7c.png[/img]

They will occur [i]on average[/i] once every 10 years (but could be much shorter or longer!). Changing the difficulty slider affects the severity of the crash. Note a few industries might still grow a little during these crashes so it's not a sign you should immediately sell everything. Also consider the tax implications if your assets have increased in value a lot.


[h3]Partying Passion[/h3]
With normal activities, the chance for your characters to invite friends and build opinion varies depending on their Social preference (25% for allergics and 300% for addicts). 

The Partying passion adds special activities that can support many more invites at once and is a great way to build more friendships in less time. Of course, your Social allergic characters will still hate every second of it but your Social addicts will have the best time of their life.

notes.title: Update Notes For v0.52.00
notes.notes:
This update is mainly about improving the asset decay system for a more accurate simulation. Previously, all your business and household assets would lose condition at a fixed rate. You'd buy a set of office computers and some years later they'd all expire at the same time.

Now some assets will only lose condition when they get used by someone. For example, a Delivery Driver spends 100% of their work hours driving so they will wear out their vehicle much faster than a Real Estate Director, who spends only 25% of their work hours driving.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44216768/85793a221d60215a93e8f50fa088cc823c63b373.png[/img]

This applies to the household and personal assets as well. When cooking food at home, the oven is only use 50% of the time. On the other hand, a Chef at a restaurant would use it 100% of the time and therefore wear out the oven sooner.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44216768/4d4498cfa5c87678164f98a4f6f170f3a2b13c40.png[/img]

It also means you can do things like buy a ton of trucks for your single person Trucking Company and not worry about them decaying prematurely.

On a separate note, I apologise to the 5.9% of Canadian players who had their maple-covered country relegated to a Steam Workshop mod. Calgary is now available in the base game, although if you're already playing the city using the workshop mod you should keep the mod enabled.

You will now be able to hire services to handle some household tasks. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44216768/f89a1e738d2d3c93f4756af1851007ea61c303dc.png[/img]

A nanny will provide babies with the presence of an adult. A home chef will do the Cook Food activity.

With some modification, I've been able to leverage the existing auto actions decision-making process to implement this feature. This means the services calculate a desire value and have the same requirements as your characters to perform their tasks. For example a home chef can't cook if your household is missing an oven and will inform you of this problem.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44216768/fd5dc781e1da8ab928ac99e0168306b0afde4479.png[/img]

These services come at a price (which fluctuates with inflation, as usual) so you'll have to consider whether the time savings are worth it for your particular circumstances.

On a separate note, I've moved a bunch of tutorials into permanent help buttons that you can access at any time on the relevant windows. It makes a lot more sense this way since you might not be interested in certain features until hours into a game!

notes.title: Update Notes For v0.45.02
notes.notes:
Hi everyone, thought I'd add more words to this post explaining why there's been no update to the game in almost 48 hours.

I've been working on a pay rise system which has been the most requested feature (or maybe it's the same person asking multiple times, I didn't check). Since this is a new system it required more time for design and testing.

The crazy 2-3 updates/day of launch week will slow down now especially when I'm working on new and bigger features instead of improving existing content.

[h3]Performance Reviews and Pay Rises[/h3]

For your regular jobs, every 12 months your character will undergo a performance review. When this happens you get some options.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44216768/c8cff4477a11873449dce58ac496cb9938ea498a.png[/img]

You can only ask for a raise or accept a bonus payment if your work performance is high enough, i.e you are skilled at the job and didn't miss too many hours of work.

The percentage raise/bonus is affected by industry inflation. Workers in a declining industry will have a much smaller potential raise than those in booming industries.
